finding.claim: Stored SSRF (blind): a callbackUrl supplied to POST /subscribe is stored without any validation, and notifyAll POSTs the payload to every stored URL every minute. An attacker can register internal targets such as http://169.254.169.254/..., http://localhost:PORT/ or RFC-1918 hosts and have the server send requests to them repeatedly. The response body is discarded, so the SSRF is blind; it still allows internal probing, port scanning and hitting internal endpoints with POSTs. The default HttpClient also does not follow redirects (the default policy is NEVER), so redirect-based pivoting is not an issue here.
finding.source: callbackUrl body parameter of POST /subscribe (Jobs.subscribe), attacker-controlled

trace.note: POST /subscribe accepts name and callbackUrl from the request body
subscriptions.put(name, callbackUrl) stores the raw URL with no scheme, host or IP validation
notifyAll iterates subscriptions.values() on a schedule (every minute)
URI.create(cb) builds the request URI from the stored, unvalidated value
client.send dispatches the POST to the attacker-chosen host

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, scheme check, hostname check or IP/CIDR block in subscribe() or notifyAll(). No re-validation at fetch time. No authentication is visible in this file; auth on the endpoint could not be checked because the routing layer is not in the repo. The JDK HttpClient default redirect policy is NEVER, so redirects are not followed.

verdict.reason: src/Jobs.java:14 stores callbackUrl unvalidated and src/Jobs.java:21-24 POSTs to it via URI.create(cb) and client.send with no scheme, host or IP checks (the only regex guard, at :30, protects thumb(), not this path); the code has no authentication, and the routing layer is not in the repo so auth on the endpoint could not be checked.
